subject: science
title: KS3 Science — Biology: Variation and Inheritance
subtitle: Revision practice on variation, inheritance, adaptation, selective breeding, extinction and working scientifically with variation data.
description: A KS3 Biology pack covering inherited and environmental variation, continuous and discontinuous data, DNA, chromosomes, genes, adaptation, selective breeding, extinction and scientific data skills. It is based on the source study pack and uses curriculum-relevant examples from humans, plants, animals, agriculture and conservation.

data.sentence: Variation means differences between individuals of the same ____.
data.hint: A group that can reproduce to produce offspring of the same kind.

data.sentence: Variation caused by genetic information from parents is called ____ variation.
data.hint: It is passed on during reproduction.

data.sentence: A scar from an accident is an example of ____ variation.
data.hint: It is caused during life.

data.sentence: Height is often affected by both inherited information and ____ during growth.
data.hint: Diet and health are examples.

data.sentence: Variation measured across a range of values is called ____ variation.
data.hint: Hand span and height are examples.

data.sentence: Blood group is ____ variation because it falls into separate categories.
data.hint: It is counted in groups.

data.sentence: DNA is found in long structures called ____ in the nucleus of most body cells.
data.hint: These structures are made from DNA.

data.sentence: A gene is a short section of ____ with instructions for an inherited characteristic.
data.hint: The chemical carrying genetic information.

data.sentence: Offspring usually receive a ____ of genetic information from their parents.
data.hint: They are not usually identical to either parent.

data.sentence: Speaking a language is a learned behaviour, not a feature passed on through ____.
data.hint: Skills are gained by experience and practice.

data.sentence: An adaptation helps an organism survive and ____ in its environment.
data.hint: Survival alone is not the full definition.

data.sentence: Migration is a ____ adaptation because it is an action.
data.hint: Actions are behaviours.

data.sentence: A streamlined fish body is a ____ adaptation because it is a body feature.
data.hint: Physical features are structural.

data.sentence: Selective breeding only works well for characteristics that are ____.
data.hint: The chosen feature must be passed to offspring.

data.sentence: A risk of selective breeding is reduced genetic ____.
data.hint: Too narrow a breeding group can make populations vulnerable.

data.sentence: Extinction means that no living members of a ____ remain anywhere on Earth.
data.hint: Moving away from one area is not global extinction.

data.sentence: In the wetland bird data, habitat area fell from 120 hectares to ____ hectares.
data.hint: Use the 2025 habitat value.

data.sentence: The independent variable in the seedling investigation was the ____ level.
data.hint: This was the factor deliberately changed.

data.sentence: The anomalous very low light seedling result was ____ cm.
data.hint: It was much taller than the other two seedlings in that group.

data.sentence: A larger sample size and more repeats usually make evidence more ____.
data.hint: They make conclusions more trustworthy.

data.title: Cell to gene organisation
data.instruction: Put the structures in order from the whole body cell to a gene.
items: Body cell
Nucleus
Chromosomes
DNA
Gene as a section of DNA with instructions

data.title: How inherited features pass on
data.instruction: Put the inheritance idea in a logical order.
items: Parents have genetic information in DNA.
Reproduction passes genetic information to offspring.
Offspring receive a mixture of genetic information.
Offspring often resemble parents but are not identical.
Environmental factors can also affect some characteristics.

data.title: Selective breeding wheat
data.instruction: Put the selective breeding process in the correct order.
items: Identify useful inherited characteristics such as high yield and disease resistance.
Choose parent plants with the useful characteristics.
Breed the chosen parent plants.
Grow and test the offspring.
Select the best offspring as parents for the next generation.
Repeat for many generations.

data.title: Pathway to extinction risk
data.instruction: Put the extinction risk sequence in order.
items: Environmental change or habitat loss occurs.
Food, shelter or breeding sites become limited.
Fewer individuals survive and reproduce.
The population falls.
If the decline continues, the species may become extinct.
